sentences.text: However, since the instant reference forwarded to this Court by the LAC only pertains to land admeasuring (24-9) falling under Khasra No.60 min, the claim of the petitioners in respect of the remaining khasra numbers cannot be entertained by this Court as being the reference Court, this Court cannot go beyond the scope of reference forwarded to it for adjudication.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon the case titled as 'Sharda Devi Vs.
State of Bihar & Anr.' dated 08.01.2003 wherein while quoting 'Nusserwanjee Pestonjee Vs. Meer Mynoodeen Khan Wullud Meer Sudroodeen Khan Bahadoor, 6 Moo Ind App134', it is so held:-
"Their Lordships of the Privy Council have held that wherever jurisdiction is given by a Statute and such jurisdiction is only given upon certain specified terms contained therein it is a universal principle that those terms should be complied with, in order to create and raise the jurisdiction, and if they are not complied with the jurisdiction does not arise.
Further, In Kothamasu Kanakarathamma and Ors. Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors. AIR 1965 SC 304, this Court held that under the Land Acquisition Act the matter goes to the Court only upon a reference made by the Collector and there is no doubt that the jurisdiction of the Court arises solely on the basis of a reference made to it.
The Court can adjudicate upon the matter referred to it but the Court is certainly not invested with the jurisdiction to consider a matter not directly connected with it and this is not a matter of mere technicality.

2.) Whether the petition is barred by limitation?

(OPR) 
a) The onus to prove this issue is upon the respondents.
However, neither any evidence has been led nor argued in this regard.

The proviso to Section 18 of L.A. Act provides for period LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 10 of 15 of limitation during which an application for reference to the Court can be made to the Collector.

entities.text: LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 10 of 15
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The same reads as under:-
"Section 18. Reference to Court:-
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made.
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award.
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, which period shall first expire".
b) Though no evidence has been led to prove this issue, however, on perusal of record, it is observed that in the instant case, award was pronounced on 22.12.1982 whereas petitioners have preferred their claim petition u/s 18 of L.A Act before LAC on 31.01.1983 as per the diary entry vide No.31/LAC MSW/31.01.1983 as mentioned on the copy of reference petition sent to this court u/s 18 of L.A Act by the LAC.
Meaning thereby, it has been filed within six weeks from the date of award and thus, within limitation.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial is brought on record on behalf of the respondents to show how the present reference is barred by limitation.
Even in the written submissions filed on behalf of respondents, no objection as to the limitation has been taken.

However, on the aspect of interest, Ld. Counsel for Union of India argued that the petitioners are not entitled to the interest on account of delay caused due to inaction on their part in bringing on record the LRs of the petitioners.

In support, counsel for Union of India has relied upon the judgments of the Hon'ble High Court in the case titled as "Jagmohan & Ors. Vs. UOI & Ors." wherein while relying upon the judgments titled as 'Kanwar Singh Vs. UOI' and 'Chander Vs. UOI' held as under:-
" 4. We have perused the judgments and orders cited and find force in the contention of learned Counsel for the respondent.

Although in the order dated 17.07.1998 of Division Bench of this Court the substitution of legal heirs was allowed without any pre condition, it appears that the Court there was not considering the question of payment of interest for the period of delay in approaching the Court for substitution.

On the other hand, the Full Bench of this Court in Chander v. UOI (supra)
made it clear that where the delay was on account of the claimant, interest for the period of delay should be declined.

5. Further in Kanwar Singh v. UOI, 120 (2005) Delhi Law Times 348 (DB) a Division Bench of this Court reiterated this LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 12 of 15 position by observing thus:
"It has been the consistent practice of this Court in a number of matters that wherever such applications have been filed belatedly, the same are allowed only subject to the restriction of non-grant of interest for the period of delay from the date of filing of the appeal till the date of filing of the application.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, by virtue of the instant reference LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 6 of 15 petition, the petitioners have claimed enhanced compensation in respect of their land bearing Khasra No.611/2 min (1-10), 60 min (1-9), 1393/838 (3-1) and 60 min (24-9).
However, since the instant reference forwarded to this Court by the LAC only pertains to land admeasuring (24-9) falling under Khasra No.60 min, the claim of the petitioners in respect of the remaining khasra numbers cannot be entertained by this Court as being the reference Court, this Court cannot go beyond the scope of reference forwarded to it for adjudication.
There can be no waiver or acquiescence.
Therefore, the market value with respect to the property in question acquired vide the same notification U/s 4 of L.A. Act dated 13.11.1959 and the main award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 11.04.1991 passed in the case titled as "Kesho Dass Vs. Union of India and Anr." 45 (1991) DLT 20, 1991 (1), DRJ Suppl 429 in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification but in main award @ Rs.8064/- per per bigha along-with statutory benefits.
b) Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, location and topography and acquired vide the main award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard since this is a supplementary award to the main award,
though the date of notification U/s 4 of L.A. Act is same.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.
c) Since no evidence has been led by the petitioners in support of their case, they are held entitled to the enhanced compensation only in respect of land acquired as stated in the statement U/s 19, L.A.
Act referred by LAC in this Court as per which land admeasuring (24-9) falling under Khasra No.60 min is acquired.
The proviso to Section 18 of L.A. Act provides for period LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 10 of 15 of limitation during which an application for reference to the Court can be made to the Collector.
The same reads as under:-
"Section 18. Reference to Court:-
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made.
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award.
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, which period shall first expire".
b) Though no evidence has been led to prove this issue, however, on perusal of record, it is observed that in the instant case, award was pronounced on 22.12.1982 whereas petitioners have preferred their claim petition u/s 18 of L.A Act before LAC on 31.01.1983 as per the diary entry vide No.31/LAC MSW/31.01.1983 as mentioned on the copy of reference petition sent to this court u/s 18 of L.A Act by the LAC.
Hence,
this issue is decided in favour LAC No.28/16 Niader Vs. Union of India Pg No. 11 of 15 of the Naidar vs Union Of India on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37897681/
7 petitioners.
Even otherwise, it is an unwarranted burden on the State Exchequer and if this practice is not curtailed, it would encourage the unscrupulous litigants to derail the proceedings on one ground or the other just to get the handsome interest @ 15% per annum which otherwise is not available on deposits in any banking sector or any other kind of deposit.
Further, whenever individual interest is pitted against the interest of society at large, the latter shall prevail.
d) Accordingly, petitioners would also be entitled to other statutory benefits i.e. solatium on the enhanced market value and interest as per the aforesaid market value in terms of judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled as 'Kesho Dass Vs. Union of India & Anr.' and interest on solatium as clarified in the decision reported as 'Sunder Vs. Union of India' DLT 1993 (2001) 569 SC.
